items.abstract: <jats:p>Stateful network protocols evolve through consecutive messages, so initial-corpus quality and message-sequence mutation directly affect deep-state exploration. Existing protocol fuzzers often suffer from re dundant seeds, weak state progression, and single-message mutations that disrupt inter-message dependencies. This paper proposes Marko vAFL, a greybox protocol fuzzer based on the protocol-controlled Markov property and message-pair correlated mutation. MarkovAFL first builds a protocol knowledge base from RFC specifications, gen erates candidate seeds through a chain linking user actions, request methods, and protocol messages, and combines runtime context, dry run validation, and behavioral deduplication to construct an effective and diverse initial corpus. During online fuzzing, it treats adjacent messages as a joint mutation unit to explore new local state-transition combinations while preserving target-state reachability. We evaluate MarkovAFL on seven text-based protocol implementations. Compared with ChatAFL, its initial corpus has lower redundancy and exposes more initial observable states and unique state transitions. Compared with AFLNet, AFLNet-Legion, and ChatAFL, MarkovAFL performs better overall in branch coverage, observable states, and unique state transition edges, with cross-implementation median improvements of approximately 4.8%, 17.8%, and 13.7%, respectively, over the strongest competitor on each implementation. These results show that chain based seed generation improves the initial exploration point, while message-pair correlated mutation strengthens local state-transition ex ploration for text-based stateful protocols.</jats:p>
title: MarkovAFL: A Greybox Protocol Fuzzing Method Based on the Protocol-Controlled Markov Property and Message-Pair Correlated Mutation
